2. Facts of the case, briefly, are that the petitioner filed Title Suit No.17 of 1991 in the Fourth Court of Assistant Judge, Narayanganj against respondent Nos.2-5 for specific performance of contract. The suit was decreed on compromise on 12-11-91 and in execution of the said decree, Title Execution Case No.2 of 1991, the petitioner got possession of the disputed property on 18-2-94. On 1-3-94 the predecessor of respondent Nos.1(a)-1(f), Krishnadhan Banik, who was not a party to Title Suit No.17 of 1991, filed an application under rule 100 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure, Miscellaneous Case No.6 of 1994, complaining that he had been illegally dispossessed from the property in execution of the decree passed in Title Suit No.17 of 1991. The said Misc. case having been allowed by judgment and order dated 14-7-1994, the petitioner instituted Title Suit No.83 of 1994 under rule 103 of Order XXI CPC which is now pending. The petitioner prayed for an order of temporary injunction restraining defendant, Krishnadhan Banik, from taking delivery of possession of the property in execution of the judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous Case No.6 of 1994. As already noticed, the prayer was rejected both by the trial Court and the appellate Court. 

 "We find that the word "shall" used in rule 101 indicate that the successful applicant must be put into possession and words "present possession" in rule 103 mean that the plaintiff in a suit filed thereunder shall have to establish his claim to get the present possession and do not mean that he shall have to establish his claim to retain his present possession, that is to say, the decree-holder has to file the suit under rule 102 for possession for deciding the question of title because in a case under rule 101 the executing court can deal only with bonafide possession of a third party dispossessed in execution of a decree and the third party, if successful, must be put into possession."
